claims.text: The starting material consists of nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt high-entropy nanoparticles.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are synthesized at room temperature.
The starting nanoparticles have a well-defined crystalline structure.
Controlled in situ heating in a high-resolution TEM can investigate the thermal behavior of the nanoparticles at atomic scale.
Heating under vacuum in increments between approximately 400 and 800 °C permits real-time monitoring of atomic-scale structural changes.
High-resolution TEM can track atomic positions, local lattice parameters, and crystallographic orientations in these nanoparticles.
Elevated temperature promotes diffusion of the constituent metal atoms.
Elevated temperature promotes rearrangement of the constituent metal atoms.
The nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt mixture has high configurational entropy.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the nanoparticle structure against thermal degradation.
In situ heating TEM will reveal temperature-induced atomic rearrangements supporting an entropy-stabilized structure.
AuCoCuNiPt high-entropy nanoparticles have enhanced thermal stability relative to conventional nanoalloys.
Controlled atomic rearrangements or phase transitions can occur while significant crystallographic order is retained.
Retention of crystallographic order during heating would confirm that entropy causes enhanced thermal stability.
Electron-beam effects can alter the observed nanoparticle structures.
Diffraction and spectroscopic analyses may be needed to validate the proposed thermodynamic stabilization mechanism.
